Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Leading the daily prayers in the mosque
Situation2: A large gathering has assembled for a special remembrance, and no one else present is authorized to lead.
Story: The air was thick with anticipation as the family holiday approached, a time when my children and grandchildren expected my presence, my stories, and my laughter. My daughter had called twice already, reminding me how much the little ones missed me, how they looked forward to our annual gathering. Yet, as the imam of our mosque, I was also bound by duty. Today, a special remembrance had drawn a large crowd, and I was the only one authorized to lead the prayers. The congregation looked to me for guidance, for comfort, for the words that would bind us together in faith. My phone buzzed in my pocket—a message from my son, asking if I would be home in time for dinner. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing on my shoulders: the warmth of my family’s embrace and the solemn responsibility to my community. My heart ached as I stood in the mosque, torn between the call of my loved ones and the call to serve.
